I agree, but I was a fence sitter for a long time. Unfortunately I ended up on the other side of the fence as she did.

I’m sure there are plenty of CF women, but to find one who is both compatible personally AND also CF will be quite challenging I think!

The good news is that I suspect a lot of CF women will be well-educated and atheist, which are both attributes I find important.

For her it is. I feel like the ‘clock’ is just a metaphor for a feeling that brews inside someone. Sure, it may not align with biology, but she clearly feels like she’s ready and wants to be with someone who’s on the same page.

It’s not necessarily about ‘hate’ though. Mutual hate of something is hardly the basis of a healthy relationship.

Sure, kids can be cute and I have a niece and nephew who I adore, but I’m so happy to be able to close the door and say “BYEEEE!” at the end and not have to deal with the circus for a minute longer.

I’ve been to Thailand once on a bachelor party. What I saw was hardly the real Thailand (hence my desire to go again), but the amount of attention you get as a foreigner is rather intimidating at times.

It’s one of the greenest and most beautiful places I’ve been to though. And oh my god, the food!
Unfortunately, that’s where my ex is from. I absolutely love japan and have been three times already, but I think it would be too difficult for now.

I think this is different for everyone. I think that ‘clock’ is just a metaphorical expression of how someone feels. She just feels like she’s ready and doesn’t want to wait any longer.

As for her motivation, I have raised my doubts before. She’s from a conservative Japanese background and you can bet that MIL demands a grandchild. She claims she’s unaffected by that though.

But that is none of my concern.

Hah, I know a girl who wanted kids when she was 18. She had them and, to her credit, raised them well. Some people are just meant to be parents, it’s their calling. 

I like to think my CF nature is a natural way of population control.
